answer: It doesn't. In node2vec, the binary operators (Average, Hadamard, Weighted-L1, Weighted-L2) combine the learned embeddings f(u) and f(v) element-wise to form the pair feature g(u,v). This is a pure function of the two vectors, so it can be computed for any pair of nodes, whether or not an edge exists between them. Edges matter only indirectly: the embeddings are learned from random walks over the graph, which encode neighborhood structure, and during link-prediction training, edges serve as positive labels while sampled non-edges serve as negatives. At inference, g(u,v) is computed for candidate pairs, including non-edges, to predict whether a link exists.
confidence_reasoning: The core fact that the operators are defined for any node pair and are applied to non-edges at prediction time follows directly from the node2vec paper's link-prediction setup, though I am recalling the details from memory.
